Title:
Untying Prefill and Decode Loops in Looped Language Models

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
16 pages, 7 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models reuse one block of layers several times per token and, under fixed-depth inference, run the same number of loops when they prefill the prompt and when they decode each answer token. We untie the two. A small loop adapter trained once on a frozen looped model lets it prefill with m loops and decode with n, for all 16 pairs up to four loops, from one stored prompt KV cache. Mapping accuracy over (m,n) on thirteen benchmarks shows that the best prefill count depends on the benchmark, its prompt and the decode budget. Within one adapter, prefilling 4-shot MATH-500 with one loop instead of four raises accuracy from 51.8 to 68.4 at four decode loops, while MMLU needs three or four prefill loops. Choosing m for each benchmark on held-out halves of its items beats the native Ouro-2.6B with the same number of decode loops significantly on 12 of 13 benchmarks with one decode loop (by 5 to 21 points) and on 10 of 13 with two; at three or four decode loops results are mixed. On Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, prefill 4 / decode 2 has higher point estimates than the native two-loop model on eight benchmarks (significantly on five), scores above a LoRA distillation of that model trained with the same data and teacher, and answers GSM8K in 0.55x the time of the native four-loop model. Untying the loops also makes looped decision models more accurate when they decide with one loop. Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode
